rubrics.criterion: The storage audit for the variable-width string family (payload bytes, row boundaries, packed validity, row count) is hosted as an operation of the string array type it summarizes, inside that type's own impl, rather than as a standalone function elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: This reporting function reads only the string family's members, so its relocation onto that family is the core of the requested cleanup in the core crate's storage layer.

rubrics.criterion: The storage audit for the descriptor-carrying decimal family (including the precision/scale metadata pair and the slot-width-based size estimate) is hosted as an operation of the decimal array type it summarizes, inside that type's own impl.
rubrics.rationale: The decimal audit derives every reported field from the decimal family's own storage and metadata accessors; only the host type can own that interpretation.

rubrics.criterion: The storage audit for the list family (child-row payload estimate, row boundaries, per-family validity representation, row count) is hosted as an operation of the list array type it summarizes, inside that type's own impl.
rubrics.rationale: The list audit's nested-payload estimation depends on list-specific knowledge, which is exactly the knowledge the family itself holds.

rubrics.criterion: The storage audit for the fixed-width 32-bit integer family (including its empty-array guard) is hosted as an operation of the integer array type it summarizes, on that family's own impl (generic host specialized for the concrete integer type is acceptable).
rubrics.rationale: The fixed-width baseline family carries the slot-width arithmetic and the empty-state guard; the audit that encodes both belongs to the family.

rubrics.criterion: The batch narration that renders one compact shape line per input column (physical kind, emptiness, leading value, row count) is hosted as functionality of the erased runtime column-view type it renders, on that type's own impl reachable from the expression shell.
rubrics.rationale: The narration is a rendering of the erased view's own answers; hosting it on the view keeps the view and its rendered shape together, which is the relation the report asks to fix in the expression layer.

rubrics.criterion: The narration that renders a bound expression's declared signature line (kernel name, declared input types, logical and physical output) is hosted as functionality of the bound-expression type it renders, on that type's own impl in the expression-binding crate.
rubrics.rationale: The signature line projects the bound object's own state; keeping the projection on the bound type is the binding-crate half of the requested cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: After the relocation, every summary remains reachable from workspace code: the crate/module wiring is updated so each relocated operation is callable through the owning crate's public surface, with no dangling module or re-export pointing at removed items.
rubrics.rationale: The compatibility boundary requires the reporting surface to stay usable; changing how the summaries are exposed is allowed, losing them behind stale wiring is not.

rubrics.criterion: The family-agnostic reporting vocabulary — the report record and the width/bit-count helpers that no particular owner owns — stays in one shared place used by the relocated audits, instead of being duplicated into each storage family.
rubrics.rationale: The change asked for is a relocation of owner-specific reading, not a stamping-out of shared vocabulary; keeping the shared pieces shared is the accompanying design obligation.

rubrics.criterion: No previous location still contains an implementation that re-derives any summary from the owner's members: relocating must actually move the authority for each reading, not leave a sibling function behind that computes the same report from the same accessors.
rubrics.rationale: A leftover same-reading sibling preserves the exact two-file drift problem the cleanup is meant to remove, even if the new host also exists.

rubrics.criterion: The stand-alone module created in the expression shell for the batch narration is removed together with its module declaration and re-export, since its entire content was relocated narration; nothing analogous remains for content that moved elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: This module existed only to host the narration; keeping a husk of it after the move leaves a misleading map of where the summaries live.

rubrics.criterion: No superseded free items or dead wiring survive the move: no orphan `mod` declaration, no re-export of a deleted path, no now-unused import, and no thin forwarding wrapper left at the old location that exists only to reproduce the pre-change call shape.
rubrics.rationale: These leftovers are what a reviewer of this cleanup would ask to be swept after the real move; they signal the restructuring stopped halfway.

rubrics.criterion: No reported value or rendered text drifts: for identical inputs, the reported storage byte counts, row and null-row counts, slot/boundary counts, family metadata pairs, and the per-line narration strings are byte-identical to what the pre-change layer produced (same contents, same field order).
rubrics.rationale: Nothing in the checked test suite exercises this reporting payload, so preservation of the summaries is a genuine regression guard rather than a redundant one.

rubrics.criterion: The relocation touches nothing adjacent that it does not need: storage-family internals, evaluation kernels and vectorization templates, builders, and the binding decision logic are edited only to the extent required by hosting the summaries.
rubrics.rationale: A heavy-handed pass that reshapes storage or binding internals to make room would change teaching code the course depends on, which the request explicitly scopes out.
